name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Open seat removes incumbent risk but no Democratic opening evidence
Republican Stigall has a large fundraising edge and outside spending
Markets price a Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: The R+19 lean makes this a heavily Republican open seat, and the Democratic nominee has raised almost nothing while the Republican has outspent him and drawn outside support. Markets price a Republican win near 95%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a scandal involving the Republican nominee, could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's open seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, and Sam Graves's retirement does little to change that. Chris Stigall enters as the clear favorite, having raised nearly $600,000 to Democrat Josh Smead's $72,000, and outside groups have spent against Smead while none have helped him.

With no public polls and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on the district's R+19 lean and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets give the Democrat only a small chance of winning. A Republican hold is expected by a wide margin, though open-seat races carry somewhat more uncertainty than contests with an incumbent on the ballot.
